eng note for a11y: 
1. Ensure the keyboard focus stays on the checkbox when it is checked/unchecked - the new content is dynamically added below and keyboard focus may be auto-dropped elsewhere (to the top of the dialog or on the underlying grayed-out page) and this would create a huge burden for all keyboard and assistive technology users. This needs to be tested, please.
2. Ensure the tooltip with the password restraint is wrapped in a `role="tooltip"` container that has `id` and this `id` is referenced by the input field via `aria-describedby`. The container should include all on-screen items from the tooltip and has `aria-labelledby` set to the "Required" heading (via `id` ref). Detailed example can be found on the Inclusive Patterns - Tooltips & Toggletips page (it is not as complex as what we have here, but the best that is reliably accessible). Lookout for/test the focus order (below)
3. Once the tooltip is visible, it has to be included in the focus and reading order right after its triggering input (ideally, it's injected in the DOM after the <input> so it's all handled "for free", but if it is not, it has to be explicitly handled in code): pressing `Tab` from the input should get the focus to the "Tips for creating strong passwords" link on the tooltip > `Tab` from it would move the focus to the next input (and tooltip is dismissed). 
4. Ensure the tooltip is shown when the input is either focused with keyboard or hovered with mouse (touch users would have to tap to activate the input and get the tooltip only then, I assume). It should stay visible while the input stays focused/hovered/active OR the tooltip itself is hovered OR the link in the tooltip "Tips for creating a strong password" is focused with keyboard.
5. Tooltip should be dismissed once a user is presses `Escape` key
6. when a field is in error, ensure it is programmatically communicated as well via "aria-describedby" referencing to the instructions/errors and "aria-invalid" 

This dialog is likely to be easy to make inaccessible for users based on the combination of complex patterns used. We all want users to be able to enjoy this crucial feature, so when in doubt, check the WAI Forms Tutorial and reach out to the Fx A11y team in #accessibility Slack/Matrix.

Please do request an engineering review from our team (in Phab during the patch work or in Bugzilla when it's locally testable in Nightly) and advocate for the review. User testing with Fable (with disabled users) is available for Firefox teams. Tooltips aren't quite a "one size fits all" thing and users have a lot of considerations when using them. Especially, when they're triggered from a modal dialogs that are adding extra layer of complexity for assistive technology to properly handle.

eng note for a11y:
1. ensure the dialog has `role=dialog` on the container and this container is also using `aria-labelledby` that refers to the `id` value of the on-screen title ("Turn on backup", in this case)

On dialog init, the focus should either move to the heading (with `tabindex="-1"` to allow the JS `.focus()` method to place the focus on the text; it is okay to not to show a focus outline in this case, while the text is focused), OR on the container itself (similarly to the heading), OR on the first focusable element ("What will be backed up?" link, in this case)
note: the focus should be managed (placed as described above) every time the dialog's content is updated.

eng notes:
1. Please ensure the instructions from the tooltip are explicitly provided for the password input field (WAI Tutorial for Inline instructions and more ideas in the Toggletips pattern).
2. most likely, the tooltip container would need `role=tooltip` and the container's own `id` value should be used on the password text input via `aria-describedby` (refer to the tooltip as additional information example, ignore the warning there since the ARIA 1.3 has been fully rolled out). So the tooltip should be announced for the password input.
3. tooltip should be dismissed when `Escape` key is pressed
4. but also the tooltip should be persistent until dismissed (i.e. if shown on hover of the text input, a user should be able to move their mouse pointer from the text input to the tooltip and a link on the tooltip without the tooltip disappearing on them)
5. show the tooltip when the Password input is focused (but do not move the focus there - it should be included in the focus order - ref next note)

eng note:
1. Checkmarks are okay to be hidden from assistive technology (to be marked up as decorative) because the on-screen text next to each image is implying the meaning for a checkmark or for a "-" minus in a text.
2. list should be marked up as a list programmatically.

eng note: ensure the focus is landed either on the "Choose...." button or on the page title. To make a static heading text focusable, add `tabindex="-1"` to it to allow the JS `.focus()` method to place the focus on the text; it is okay to not to show a focus outline in this case, while the text is focused. Focus should become visible once a user presses `Tab` key (and the focus is visibly placed on "Choose..." button)

There are existing `access-S2` bugs in similar transitions from a dialog to an about:page when the focus was not managed proactively and it is lost or is landed somewhere in the middle of the content. Users of screen readers have been confused with it and are often not aware that there is, in fact, new content being shown (refer to the Intro to A11y course by Fable on makeitfable.com (use your SSO to log in) to view the video recording of a desktop user in a similar situation)

eng note:
1. each card should be grouped together. I.e. the container would have `role=group` and would get `aria-labelledby` to be set to the `id` value of the on-screen card title ("Sync with Firefox" and "Back up to PC", in this case).
2. Additionally, we could add `aria-describedby` to the `role=group` container and refer this to the container itself (one starting with "Recommended", another one with "Back up to PC",  both ending with "Select").
This would allow all the content inside the group, including the "Select" buttons to have their own context and be announced together, once a screen reader would focus a button.

eng note: 
1. images should be marked up as decorative since the text next to each one of them is implying the yes/no meaning in-text, thus the images would be providing redundant information, if exposed to assistive technology.
2. Ideally, the options would be marked up as a list
3. for the bold text, using `<strong>` HTML element is recommended since it would expose the styling to a screen reader (while CSS styling, for instance, would be ignored by the major assistive technology)

a11y.message:
eng note for a11y: 
1. Ensure the keyboard focus stays on the checkbox when it is checked/unchecked - the new content is dynamically added below and keyboard focus may be auto-dropped elsewhere (to the top of the dialog or on the underlying grayed-out page) and this would create a huge burden for all keyboard and assistive technology users. This needs to be tested, please.
2. Ensure the tooltip with the password restraint is wrapped in a `role="tooltip"` container that has `id` and this `id` is referenced by the input field via `aria-describedby`. The container should include all on-screen items from the tooltip and has `aria-labelledby` set to the "Required" heading (via `id` ref). Detailed example can be found on the Inclusive Patterns - Tooltips & Toggletips page (it is not as complex as what we have here, but the best that is reliably accessible). Lookout for/test the focus order (below)
3. Once the tooltip is visible, it has to be included in the focus and reading order right after its triggering input (ideally, it's injected in the DOM after the <input> so it's all handled "for free", but if it is not, it has to be explicitly handled in code): pressing `Tab` from the input should get the focus to the "Tips for creating strong passwords" link on the tooltip > `Tab` from it would move the focus to the next input (and tooltip is dismissed). 
4. Ensure the tooltip is shown when the input is either focused with keyboard or hovered with mouse (touch users would have to tap to activate the input and get the tooltip only then, I assume). It should stay visible while the input stays focused/hovered/active OR the tooltip itself is hovered OR the link in the tooltip "Tips for creating a strong password" is focused with keyboard.
5. Tooltip should be dismissed once a user is presses `Escape` key
6. when a field is in error, ensure it is programmatically communicated as well via "aria-describedby" referencing to the instructions/errors and "aria-invalid" 

This dialog is likely to be easy to make inaccessible for users based on the combination of complex patterns used. We all want users to be able to enjoy this crucial feature, so when in doubt, check the WAI Forms Tutorial and reach out to the Fx A11y team in #accessibility Slack/Matrix.

Please do request an engineering review from our team (in Phab during the patch work or in Bugzilla when it's locally testable in Nightly) and advocate for the review. User testing with Fable (with disabled users) is available for Firefox teams. Tooltips aren't quite a "one size fits all" thing and users have a lot of considerations when using them. Especially, when they're triggered from a modal dialogs that are adding extra layer of complexity for assistive technology to properly handle.

eng note for a11y:
1. ensure the dialog has `role=dialog` on the container and this container is also using `aria-labelledby` that refers to the `id` value of the on-screen title ("Turn on backup", in this case)
2. On dialog init, the focus should either move to the heading (with `tabindex="-1"` to allow the JS `.focus()` method to place the focus on the text; it is okay to not to show a focus outline in this case, while the text is focused), OR on the container itself (similarly to the heading), OR on the first focusable element ("What will be backed up?" link, in this case)
note: the focus should be managed (placed as described above) every time the dialog's content is updated.

eng note for a11y:
when a field is in error, ensure it is programmatically communicated as well via "aria-describedby" referencing to the instructions/errors and "aria-invalid" (follow the WAI Tutorial for guidance)

eng notes:
1. Please ensure the instructions from the tooltip are explicitly provided for the password input field (WAI Tutorial for Inline instructions and more ideas in the Toggletips pattern).
2. most likely, the tooltip container would need `role=tooltip` and the container's own `id` value should be used on the password text input via `aria-describedby` (refer to the tooltip as additional information example, ignore the warning there since the ARIA 1.3 has been fully rolled out). So the tooltip should be announced for the password input.
3. tooltip should be dismissed when `Escape` key is pressed
4. but also the tooltip should be persistent until dismissed (i.e. if shown on hover of the text input, a user should be able to move their mouse pointer from the text input to the tooltip and a link on the tooltip without the tooltip disappearing on them)
5. show the tooltip when the Password input is focused (but do not move the focus there - it should be included in the focus order - ref next note)
6. Focus the "Tips for creating strong passwords" link, when `tab` key is pressed from the Password field

Having the requirements inline would be the most accessible option and, most likely, would require much less engineering efforts to make the information accessible, so if this is possible - yay! A11y vote goes in support of this stretch goal.

eng note:
1. Checkmarks are okay to be hidden from assistive technology (to be marked up as decorative) because the on-screen text next to each image is implying the meaning for a checkmark or for a "-" minus in a text.
2. list should be marked up as a list programmatically.

eng note: ensure the focus is landed either on the "Choose...." button or on the page title. To make a static heading text focusable, add `tabindex="-1"` to it to allow the JS `.focus()` method to place the focus on the text; it is okay to not to show a focus outline in this case, while the text is focused. Focus should become visible once a user presses `Tab` key (and the focus is visibly placed on "Choose..." button)

There are existing `access-S2` bugs in similar transitions from a dialog to an about:page when the focus was not managed proactively and it is lost or is landed somewhere in the middle of the content. Users of screen readers have been confused with it and are often not aware that there is, in fact, new content being shown (refer to the Intro to A11y course by Fable on makeitfable.com (use your SSO to log in) to view the video recording of a desktop user in a similar situation)

eng note:
1. each card should be grouped together. I.e. the container would have `role=group` and would get `aria-labelledby` to be set to the `id` value of the on-screen card title ("Sync with Firefox" and "Back up to PC", in this case).
2. Additionally, we could add `aria-describedby` to the `role=group` container and refer this to the container itself (one starting with "Recommended", another one with "Back up to PC",  both ending with "Select").
This would allow all the content inside the group, including the "Select" buttons to have their own context and be announced together, once a screen reader would focus a button.

eng note: 
1. images should be marked up as decorative since the text next to each one of them is implying the yes/no meaning in-text, thus the images would be providing redundant information, if exposed to assistive technology.
2. Ideally, the options would be marked up as a list
3. for the bold text, using `<strong>` HTML element is recommended since it would expose the styling to a screen reader (while CSS styling, for instance, would be ignored by the major assistive technology)

eng note: 
each card should be grouped together. I.e. the container would have `role=group` and would get `aria-labelledby` to be set to the `id` value of the on-screen card title ("Easy setup" and "All data", in this case).
